title: This Day in Esoteric Political History

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Anyone who has listened to this show knows that I love stories from history.
sentences.zh: 听过这个节目的朋友都知道我喜欢历史故事。

sentences.en: And one of the things I love the most is that a history story in and of itself has a certain value.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一点是，历史故事本身就具有一定的价值。

sentences.en: But what's amazing is how much the current situation that you're hearing the story affects how it's understood.
sentences.zh: 但神奇的是，你听到这个故事时的当前处境，会极大程度地影响你对它的理解。

sentences.en: It's like adding a musical score to a scene in a movie.
sentences.zh: 这就好比为电影里的某个场景配上一段音乐。

sentences.en: The mood of the current moment changes our interpretation of everything.
sentences.zh: 当下的心境会改变我们对一切事物的解读。

sentences.en: This is all leading me to introducing you to a brand new history show that we have premiering today from Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了向大家介绍一档全新的历史节目，今天开始在Radiotopia首播。

sentences.en: It's produced and hosted by the immensely talented and recently mustachioed Jody Avergan,
sentences.zh: 它的制作人和主持人是才华横溢、最近还留了小胡子的乔迪·阿维根，

sentences.en: who you may know from ESPN's 30 for 30 podcast, and he was the host of the 538 Politics podcast for many years.
sentences.zh: 你可能从ESPN的《30 for 30》播客中认识他，他曾多年主持538政论播客。

sentences.en: I am a huge fan of Jody.
sentences.zh: 我是乔迪的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I'm so excited he's joining the team.
sentences.zh: 他能加入团队，我太高兴了。

sentences.en: And so on this episode, I'll talk with him and premiere two episodes of his new podcast, This Day in Esoteric Political History.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一期节目中，我将与他对话，并首播他的新播客《晦涩政治史上的今天》的两集内容。

sentences.en: Hey, Jody.
sentences.zh: 嘿，乔迪。

sentences.en: Hello there, Roman.
sentences.zh: 你好，罗曼。

sentences.en: So for context, we're talking on Friday, March 27th, each in our respective homes, me in California, you in New York City.
sentences.zh: 为了提供背景，我们是在3月27日星期五录制的，各自在自己的家里，我在加州，你在纽约市。

sentences.en: And we're going to talk about your new show on Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊聊你在Radiotopia的新节目。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm really excited to join Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 我真的很高兴能加入Radiotopia。

sentences.en: I just want to confirm, though, I'm recording in my bedroom, which has two windows.
sentences.zh: 我只想确认一下，我是按在我的卧室里录音的，这里有两扇窗户。

sentences.en: You're recording in your bedroom, which I believe listeners learned in a previous episode, has five windows.
sentences.zh: 而你是在你的卧室里录音，如果我没记错的话，听众在之前的节目中得知你有五扇窗户。

sentences.en: It has five windows.
sentences.zh: 我有五扇窗户。

sentences.en: I live on the corner, and my bedroom is on the corner of the house.
sentences.zh: 我住在转角，我的卧室在房子的转角处。

sentences.en: And so it has five windows, which makes it very good for sun, very bad for recording, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 所以它有五扇窗户，老实说，这对于采光非常好，但对于录音非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I thought both of those things.
sentences.zh: 这两点我都有想到。

sentences.en: I got immediately jealous, and then I got immediately started to do the calculus of,
sentences.zh: 我一开始超级嫉妒，然后我马上开始盘算：

sentences.en: how is he making this room quiet?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么让这个房间安静下来的？

sentences.en: But it was brave of you to admit, it was brave of you to admit as much on a national radio show.
sentences.zh: 不过你敢在全国广播节目中承认这一点，还挺勇敢的。

sentences.en: But anyway, the task at hand.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，说回正事。

sentences.en: Yes, I'm joining Radiotopia, which I'm incredibly excited about.
sentences.zh: 是的，我要加入Radiotopia了，我对此感到兴奋不已。

sentences.en: We're doing a new show that's called This Day in Esoteric Political History.
sentences.zh: 我们在做一个新节目，叫做《晦涩政治史上的今天》。

sentences.en: Basically, a couple times a week, I'm going to get together with a historian, Nicole Hemmer,
sentences.zh: 基本上，每周会有几次，我和历史学家妮可·海默聚在一起，

sentences.en: and we're going to have special guests along the way as well,
sentences.zh: 路上我们也会邀请一些特别嘉宾，

sentences.en: and look at one item, one moment that happened on that day in political history.
sentences.zh: 然后研究政治史上那天发生的一件物品、一个时刻。

sentences.en: And the show is going to be short.
sentences.zh: 而且节目会很短。

sentences.en: It's going to be under 10 minutes each time.
sentences.zh: 每次都在10分钟以内。

sentences.en: And we're just going to try and kind of pick a bunch of moments, big and small,
sentences.zh: 我们只是想挑选一堆大大小小的时刻，

sentences.en: that are either interesting stories, but I suspect we'll also have some things to teach us about
sentences.zh: 它们要么是很有趣的故事，但我猜也会有一些内容能让我们认识到

sentences.en: this moment that we're going through right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在经历的这个时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things I've noticed in the conversation about coronavirus and even Trump,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在关于冠状病毒甚至特朗普的讨论中，我注意到的一点是——

sentences.en: as we've been talking about Trump for the past couple of years,
sentences.zh: 正如我们在过去几年里一直在谈论特朗普那样——

sentences.en: is we've been falling back on this idea that all this is unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 我们一直退回到这样一种观点：这一切都是史无前例的。

sentences.en: And I think that helps describe the enormity of everything,
sentences.zh: 我想这有助于描述一切的严重程度，

sentences.en: but I don't think that description is very helpful beyond that.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我觉得这种描述并没有多大帮助。

sentences.en: I think it's a much more useful approach to find, you know, little threads of connections
sentences.zh: 我认为更有用的方法是去寻找，你知道的，那些有前例可循的细微联系线索，

sentences.en: that are precedented so that we can continue to learn and evolve and respond.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能继续学习、演变和应对。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm really excited about this day in esoteric political history.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对《晦涩政治史上的今天》感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: How do you see the role of the things that you will tell stories about
sentences.zh: 你如何看待你将讲述的故事的角色，

sentences.en: and how they connect with the modern world?
sentences.zh: 以及它们如何与现代世界相连接？

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's born of the very same instinct that I think a lot of people have had,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为它源于许多人都有的同一种本能，

sentences.en: and I've had both as a journalist and just as a human being,
sentences.zh: 无论作为记者还是作为一个普通人，我也有过这种本能，

sentences.en: to find myself thinking long before coronavirus, you know, over the last four or five years or so,
sentences.zh: 在冠状病毒爆发很久之前，你知道的，在过去四五年左右的时间里，我发现自己一直在想：

sentences.en: saying, man, this feels new.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这感觉真新鲜。

sentences.en: This feels unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 这感觉史无前例。

sentences.en: It feels like we're in completely new territory.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们正处于完全陌生的领域。

sentences.en: And I think like a lot of people, I have found myself turning to history more and more
sentences.zh: 我想和很多人一样，我发现自己越来越转向历史，

sentences.en: to get some guidance and get some guardrails.
sentences.zh: 以获得一些指导和保护栏。

sentences.en: And, you know, I've come to think that there's kind of basically three main ways
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我开始认为历史基本上可以通过三种主要方式

sentences.en: in which history can help us understand this moment.
sentences.zh: 来帮助我们理解当下的时刻。

sentences.en: And one is to say, no, this isn't new.
sentences.zh: 第一种是说，不，这并不新鲜。

sentences.en: This has happened before.
sentences.zh: 这以前发生过。

sentences.en: Look at, you know, this time, this time, and this time when basically this exact thing happened before.
sentences.zh: 你看，你知道的，这个时期、那个时期，还有那个时期，基本上完全相同的事情以前发生过。

sentences.en: And there's comfort in that.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一种安慰。

sentences.en: There really is.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: That's not to diminish the sort of seriousness of what's happening now or a given incident.
sentences.zh: 这并不是要贬低现在正在发生的事情或某起事件的严重性。

sentences.en: Then there's the second category, which is, oh, no, this really is new.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二类，那就是，哦，不，这真的是崭新的。

sentences.en: And there are moments like that.
sentences.zh: 确实有这样的时刻。

sentences.en: And I don't want to dismiss that, you know, but I think understanding when you need to raise the alarm
sentences.zh: 我不想抹杀这一点，你知道的，但我认为理解什么时候需要敲响警钟

sentences.en: and say, oh, my gosh, we are in uncharted territory.
sentences.zh: 并说，哦，天哪，我们正处于未知的领域。

sentences.en: The third category is the one that I'm really fascinated by, and I think I've really come around to,
sentences.zh: 第三类是我真正着迷的，也是我真正转变观念并想要在这档节目中探索的类别，那就是：事情可能是新的。

sentences.en: and I think I want to try and explore in this show, which is things may be new.
sentences.zh: 我们可能身处未知的领域，但这个时刻是历史的产物。

sentences.en: We may be in uncharted territory, but this moment is a product of history.
sentences.zh: 过去20、30、50、100年在这个国家积聚的种种条件，把我们带到了这一刻。

sentences.en: The conditions that have built up in this country over the last 20, 30, 50, 100 years have led us to this moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这就是我们谈论得不够多的事情：为什么我们所感受到的完全是新鲜的、

sentences.en: And that, I think, is the thing we don't talk about enough, how what we are feeling is completely new
sentences.zh: 史无前例的、仿佛凭空出现的东西，实际上正是这个国家过去发生的事情的产物。

sentences.en: and unprecedented and sort of out of nowhere is actually a product of what has happened in this country.
sentences.zh: 鉴于过去几代人塑造这个国家政治的力量，这是几乎不可避免的。

sentences.en: And it's almost inevitable, given the forces that have shaped politics in this country over the last, you know, few generations.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: That would be a pretty mess that day.
sentences.zh: 确实会。

sentences.en: It would be.
sentences.zh: 确实会。

sentences.en: It would be.
sentences.zh: 而且当时在越南问题上，局势已经相当严峻了。

sentences.en: And things were pretty dire when it came to Vietnam at that point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就在几个月前，春节攻势发动了，这真正向美国人表明战争并没有按他们的意愿发展，

sentences.en: I mean, just a few months earlier, the Tet Offensive had been launched, which really showed Americans that the war was not going their way,
sentences.zh: 而且军方和政治领导人也没有对他们说关于战争的实话。

sentences.en: and also that military and political leaders weren't telling them the truth about the war.
sentences.zh: 这确实对约翰逊的支持率产生了影响。

sentences.en: And that had a real effect on Johnson's approval ratings.
sentences.zh: 当时他正开始竞选连任，演讲时的支持率大约只有百分之三十的人支持他。

sentences.en: Here he is starting up his bid for re-election, and his approval ratings at the time of the speech were something like 30 percent of people approved of him.
sentences.zh: 真的很低。

sentences.en: It was really low.
sentences.zh: 但后来当他宣布不寻求连任时会发生什么？

sentences.en: But then what happens when he announces that he's not going to seek re-election?
sentences.zh: 突然之间，人们都爱戴他了。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, people love him.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Once they know they don't have to put up with him anymore, Americans flip.
sentences.zh: 一旦美国人知道他们再也不用忍受他了，态度就会大变。

sentences.en: They go from 57 percent disapproving of him to 57 percent of them approving of him.
sentences.zh: 他们对他的不满意度从57%直接变成了满意度57%。

sentences.en: Yes, that would not happen today.
sentences.zh: 是的，这种事如今不会发生了。

sentences.en: I mean, you look at approval ratings, and they're so steady,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看看支持率，它们是如此稳定，

sentences.en: and they're so dictated by polarization and partisanship that I don't think we will see swings like that that inherently mean people are crossing party lines in their approval.
sentences.zh: 并且深受极化和党派之争的左右，以至于我认为我们不会再看到那种本质上意味着人们跨党派支持的巨大摇摆。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's been the remarkable thing about the Trump presidency is how stable his approval ratings have been throughout.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，特朗普总统任期内最引人注目的事情，就是他的支持率在整个任期内都非常稳定。

sentences.en: If you go back earlier in the mid-20th century, you saw wide ranges of approval, and you saw presidents like Dwight Eisenhower, who was a Republican,
sentences.zh: 如果你回溯到20世纪中叶的早期，你会发现广泛的支持率波动，而且你会看到像德怀特·艾森豪威尔这样身为共和党人的总统，

sentences.en: pretty regularly getting 70 percent public approval.
sentences.zh: 相当经常地获得70%的公众支持率。

sentences.en: So it was a very, very different time then.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一个非常、非常不同的时代。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in his remarks, he kind of hints at this thing that got me thinking about the fact that he has to focus on all of the challenges before him,
sentences.zh: 所以在他的发言中，他暗示了一件事，让我开始思考这样一个事实：他必须专注于他面前的所有挑战，

sentences.en: and then he is also being asked to run for re-election.
sentences.zh: 然后他还要面临竞选连任的要求。

sentences.en: And he basically says, I can't do both of these things, so I am going to try and do my job until the end of this year, and someone else can decide to campaign.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，这两件事我无法兼顾，所以我要努力工作到今年年底，至于竞选就由别人决定吧。

sentences.en: What does it mean that we ask these presidents to campaign in their last year in this way?
sentences.zh: 我们要求这些总统在他们任期的最后一年以这种方式参与竞选，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: You know, the crises of the world don't care that it's an election year.
sentences.zh: 要知道，世界的危机可不会管这到底是不是大选年。

sentences.en: They just show up, and they can show up in the last year of a presidency as easily as they can show up in the first year.
sentences.zh: 它们说来就来，在总统任期的最后一年出现，就像在第一年出现一样容易。

sentences.en: It's an extreme challenge to both juggle the presidency, which in the right hands is a full-time job, and then layer over campaigning on top of it.
sentences.zh: 既要兼顾总统职务——如果在得力的人手里，这是一份全职工作——还要在此基础上面对竞选，这绝对是一个极大的挑战。

sentences.en: It's hard to do both really well and to not confuse the two.
sentences.zh: 要把这两件事都做好、并且不把它们混为一谈，是非常困难的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's where people often get in trouble is when you have to deal with a major crisis,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为人们往往正是在这种时候陷入麻烦：当你不得不应对一场重大危机时，

sentences.en: but now you also have to go speak to deep-pocketed donors at a $5,000 fundraiser somewhere.
sentences.zh: 但现在你还得去某个地方的五千美元筹款会上对那些腰缠万贯的捐款人发表演讲。

sentences.en: Certainly, I think we have a president now who thinks he's at his best when he's in campaigning mode, and I think thinks of everything basically as a campaign.
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为我们现在的这位总统，他觉得自己处于竞选状态时才是最好的，而且我认为他基本上把所有事情都看作是一场竞选。

sentences.en: Has anyone ever tried to, like, split these two?
sentences.zh: 有没有人尝试过，比如，把这两件事分开？

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 有点像吧。

sentences.en: So if we think about the Obama re-election campaign in 2012, he took his entire sort of re-election campaign, and he sent all of his people to Chicago,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们回想2012年奥巴马的连任竞选，他把他的整个连任竞选团队，把所有人都派去了芝加哥，

sentences.en: and they were going to run the re-election from there, and he was going to be governing in D.C.
sentences.zh: 他们将从那里运作连任，而他则要在华盛顿特区进行执政。

sentences.en: And I think that that kind of splitting, there's only so much that you can do, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这种分离，你所能做到的也只有那么多，对吧？

sentences.en: It's ultimately a fiction, but that's one attempt to do it.
sentences.zh: 这归根结底是一种虚构，但那是尝试这样做的举措之一。

sentences.en: I want to wrap up with a kind of big question about 1968 and these other moments in history that feel incredibly tumultuous.
sentences.zh: 我想以一个关于1968年以及历史上其他那些感觉极其动荡的时刻的大问题来作结。

sentences.en: So you look at 1968 and you say, goodness, you know, wars, riots, assassinations, presidents not running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 所以你看看1968年，你会说，天哪，你知道的，战争、骚乱、暗杀、总统不参加连任竞选。

sentences.en: Some of these are obviously linked to each other,
sentences.zh: 其中一些显然是相互关联的，

sentences.en: but I guess I'm trying to figure out whether there are just these eras of overall instability where it's just one of those years in which big, messy,
sentences.zh: 但我想我是在试图弄清楚，是否真的存在这样一些整体不稳定的时代，在这些年份里，重大的、混乱的、

sentences.en: epic things are going to happen, maybe even if they aren't directly tied to each other.
sentences.zh: 史诗般的事情就是会发生，哪怕它们可能并非直接相互关联。

sentences.en: Do these things kind of tend to group?
sentences.zh: 这些事情往往会成群出现吗？

sentences.en: So that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: The answer is sort of yes and no.
sentences.zh: 答案可以说是，也可以说不是。

sentences.en: I'm not sure that the assassination of Martin Luther King led to the assassination of Bobby Kennedy, but if we take a kind of bigger picture look at things,
sentences.zh: 我不确定马丁·路德·金的遇刺是否导致了罗伯特·肯尼迪的遇刺，但如果我们从更宏观的角度来看待事情，

sentences.en: instead of looking just at 68, like look at the 60s as a whole, there had been a lot of fractures forming for the whole decade, right?
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅盯着68年，而是看看整个60年代，整个十年里其实已经形成了大量的裂痕，对吧？

sentences.en: You had the Cuban Missile Crisis, which had the whole world on the brink of nuclear apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 你经历过古巴导弹危机，它把整个世界推到了核毁灭的边缘。

sentences.en: You had the assassination of John Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 你经历了约翰·肯尼迪的遇刺。

sentences.en: You had the civil rights movement and racist murders and violence that were happening pretty regularly, urban uprisings.
sentences.zh: 你经历了民权运动、相当频繁发生的种族主义谋杀和暴力事件，以及城市起义。

sentences.en: So by the time 1968 rolls around, a lot of the things that happen are kind of overdetermined because of all of these fractures that had been caused earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以在1968年到来之际，发生的许多事情在某种程度上都是注定的，因为之前已经造成了所有这些裂痕。

sentences.en: I remember in 2016, we had a few conversations on the FiveThirtyEight Politics podcast, which I did during that election.
sentences.zh: 我记得在2016年，我们在《五三十八》政治播客上进行过几次对话，那是我在选举期间做的节目。

sentences.en: That were basically, is this 1968?
sentences.zh: 基本上都在探讨：这会是1968年吗？

sentences.en: And I think what I'm realizing in retrospect was that, you know, 2016 was not our 1968.
sentences.zh: 我想我事后意识到的是，你知道，2016年并不是我们的1968年。

sentences.en: It was the beginning of the sort of process that you just described.
sentences.zh: 它只是你刚刚描述的那种进程的开始。

sentences.en: And maybe now, four years later, we're having our 1968.
sentences.zh: 也许现在，四年后，我们正在经历我们的1968年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you think about all of the things people have pointed to as weaknesses in the American system revealed by 2016,
sentences.zh: 如果你想想人们指出的、2016年所暴露出的美国体制中的所有弱点，

sentences.en: we're now in a moment with a pandemic where all of those weaknesses are starting to cause even bigger and more catastrophic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正处于一场大流行病之中，所有这些弱点都开始引发更大、更具灾难性的问题。

sentences.en: Well, on that cheery note, we will end our first episode.
sentences.zh: 好吧，带着这个轻松愉快的心情，我们将结束我们的第一集。

sentences.en: That is it for today.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目就到这里。

sentences.zh: 妮可，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Jodi.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，乔迪。

sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.zh: 我认为我不应该把哪怕一小时或一天的时间投入到除了本办公室这崇高职责之外的任何其他职责上。

sentences.zh: 广告之后，我们将全球首播《深奥政治历史上的今天》的另一完整单集，

sentences.en: and more conversation with Jody Avergan after this.
sentences.zh: 并与乔迪·阿维甘展开更多对话。

sentences.en: So could you describe the second episode, which is really relevant to the time we're in right now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能描述一下第二集吗？它与我们当前所处的时代非常相关。

sentences.en: Yeah, so our second episode, which is coming out on Thursday, April 2nd, we'll play it for people here now,
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的第二集将于4月2日星期四播出，我们现在就在这里播放给大家听，

sentences.en: is about when Woodrow Wilson got the flu in 1918 as part of the influenza pandemic of 1918.
sentences.zh: 讲的是伍德罗·威尔逊在1918年流感大流行期间于1918年染上流感的故事。

sentences.en: Actually, he got it in 1919 on April 2nd.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他是在1919年4月2日感染的。

sentences.en: This is where I should confess that we were originally planning this show to be about just elections.
sentences.zh: 在这里我应该坦白，我们最初计划这个节目时，内容只关于选举。

sentences.en: We thought this was going to be a tumultuous election year, and we thought we'd do stories from previous elections.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这将是一个动荡的大选年，我们打算讲述历届选举的故事。

sentences.en: And then we did sort of change a little bit when the coronavirus pandemic began to feel like, you know what,
sentences.zh: 然后，当冠状病毒大流行开始时，我们稍微做了一些改变，觉得你知道吗，

sentences.en: we want to make space for other stories in politics, other moments of crisis, other moments when this country has faced things like this.
sentences.zh: 我们想为政治领域的其他故事、其他危机时刻、这个国家曾经面对过类似境况的其他时刻留出空间。

sentences.en: And so we've broadened the scope a little bit, and this is an example of a kind of thing that wasn't necessarily an election year,
sentences.zh: 所以我们稍微拓宽了范围，这是一个不一定发生在大选年、

sentences.en: but obviously a moment when our politics had to react to a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但显然是我们的政治必须对大流行病作出反应的时刻的例子。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think one simple reminder is that Wilson got the flu, the president of the United States got the flu,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一个简单的提醒就是，威尔逊得了流感，美国总统得了流感，

sentences.en: basically a full year after the pandemic had started.
sentences.zh: 基本上是在大流行爆发整整一年之后。

sentences.en: And it's a simple reminder that these things come in waves and these things go for a while.
sentences.zh: 这是一个简单的提醒：这些事情是一波接一波地来，而且会持续一段时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay, let's hear it.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们来听听看。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to This Day in Esoteric Political History from Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听来自Radiotopia的《深奥政治历史上的今天》。

sentences.en: My name is Jody Avergan.
sentences.zh: 我是乔迪·阿维甘。

sentences.en: This day, April 2nd, 1919, Woodrow Wilson has the flu.
sentences.zh: 今天，1919年4月2日，伍德罗·威尔逊患上了流感。

sentences.en: The influenza pandemic is sometimes called the 1918 flu pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这场流感大流行有时被称为1918年流感大流行。

sentences.en: It started in spring 1918, but it was the second wave, as we are all learning,
sentences.zh: 它始于1918年春天，但正如我们大家所了解的那样，是1918年秋天的第二波疫情最具毁灭性，

sentences.en: in the fall of 1918 that was the most devastating, with the disease spreading into 1919.
sentences.zh: 疾病一直蔓延到了1919年。

sentences.en: That is when President Wilson reportedly caught the flu either right before or right after he arrived in Paris
sentences.zh: 据报道，正是在那时，威尔逊总统在抵达巴黎的前夕或刚到巴黎之后不久染上了流感，

sentences.en: for another round of talks to try and bring an end to the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他当时去巴黎是为了参加又一轮会谈，试图促成第一次世界大战的结束。

sentences.en: We're joined, as always, by Nicole Hemmer of Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 与往常一样，加入我们的是哥伦比亚大学的妮可·海默。

sentences.en: I'll lay out what we know and don't know about this moment in a second.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会列出我们对这段时期的了解与未知之处。

sentences.en: But we should say right off the bat, Nikki, that there's a little bit of controversy about whether he actually had the flu or there were some other things going on.
sentences.zh: 但我们应该开门见山地说，尼基，关于他到底是得了流感还是有其他情况，其实存在一些争议。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So one of the things that people know about Wilson and his health is that he suffers a pretty serious stroke near the end of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对威尔逊和他的健康的了解之一，就是他在总统任期接近尾声时遭遇了一次相当严重的中风。

sentences.en: So for a long time, historians talked about this illness as a mini stroke that he had had.
sentences.zh: 因此，很长一段时间以来，历史学家们都将这场疾病称为他曾有过的一次轻微中风。

sentences.en: But if you actually look at the set of symptoms that he had, including a really high fever, none of them really fit a stroke.
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的看看他当时的一系列症状，包括极高的发烧，没有一个症状真正符合中风。

sentences.en: And they all sound a whole lot like this pandemic that was ravaging the world at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且它们听起来非常像当时正在肆虐全球的大流行病。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, by all accounts, and we'll talk a little bit about what the ramifications of this were,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根据各方说法——我们稍后会讨论这带来的后果是什么——

sentences.en: but he was very out of it.
sentences.zh: 但他当时非常神志不清。

sentences.en: He was fever struck.
sentences.zh: 他高烧不退。

sentences.en: He was sort of deteriorating rapidly over the course of these negotiations in Paris.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎的这些谈判过程中，他的状况某种程度上在急剧恶化。

sentences.en: One thing that's interesting is that it was it was underplayed at the time, I guess.
sentences.zh: 有趣的一点是，当时它被淡化了，我猜。

sentences.en: You know, there was these questions about whether it was actually flu.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时存在着这到底是不是流感的疑问。

sentences.en: But did they try and cover this up or was it just that sort of reports were murky?
sentences.zh: 但他们是试图掩盖这一点，还是说当时的报道本来就很模糊不清？

sentences.en: Like what did people know at the time?
sentences.zh: 就像当时的人们都知道些什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when this was first reported, it was just reported that he had a cold.
sentences.zh: 所以当这件事最初被报道时，仅仅报道说他得了感冒。

sentences.en: And this probably isn't surprising.
sentences.zh: 这可能并不令人意外。

sentences.en: I mean, was it a cover up?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场掩盖吗？

sentences.en: You know, they didn't often tell in detail the kinds of illnesses that presidents had at the time.
sentences.zh: 要知道，当时他们通常不会详细说明总统所患疾病的种类。

sentences.en: There's a much bigger cover up that will happen later in his presidency about his health conditions.
sentences.zh: 在他的总统任期后期，关于他的健康状况将会有一场规模大得多的掩盖行动。

sentences.en: But in this case, not wanting to scare people in the midst of both a war and a pandemic,
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，为了在战争和大流行病夹击之际不惊吓到人们，

sentences.en: they decided to just say, hey, it's a cold.
sentences.zh: 他们决定只是说：嘿，这只是感冒。

sentences.en: He'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 他会没事的。

sentences.en: So I want to get to some of the sort of bigger questions around this, because for one, I mean,
sentences.zh: 所以我想探讨一些围绕此事的更大问题，因为首先，我的意思是，

sentences.en: it's really kind of stunning how precarious of a situation this is.
sentences.zh: 这种情况的岌岌可危程度真的是惊人的。

sentences.en: We have a leader at a meeting with all of the what is known as the big four who are negotiating the end of World War I.
sentences.zh: 我们有一位领导人正在参加一个会议，与所有被称为“四巨头”、正在谈判结束第一次世界大战的人坐在一起。

sentences.en: Wilson's doctor says, quote, the whole of civilization seemed to hang in the balance.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊的医生说，引述：“整个文明似乎都悬于一线。”

sentences.en: Is that a doctor being a little dramatic when he's writing his memoirs?
sentences.zh: 那是医生在写回忆录时有点大惊小怪吗？

sentences.en: Or I mean, is this one of really one of those moments?
sentences.zh: 还是说——我的意思是，这真的是那种历史时刻吗？

sentences.en: This is really one of those moments.
sentences.zh: 这确实是那种时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, here it is after the most devastating war that the world really had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是在经历过世界所见过的最具毁灭性的战争之后发生的。

sentences.en: And now they're trying to figure out how to bring it to a close.
sentences.zh: 现在他们正试图找出如何结束这场战争的方法。

sentences.en: And somebody like Wilson would have been the perfect person to have at that table.
sentences.zh: 而像威尔逊这样的人本该是坐在那张谈判桌前的完美人选。

sentences.en: This is something he had been thinking about, how to win the peace for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 这是他一直在思考的事情，关于如何赢得和平，他已经思考了很长一段时间。

sentences.en: And now he shows up at the peace table and he's kind of a mess.
sentences.zh: 现在他出现在了和平谈判桌前，却成了一团糟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I mean, it's like it comes down to the fact that he just can't concentrate as well as he normally would.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，归根结底就是他无法像平时那样集中注意力。

sentences.en: You know, he just doesn't he doesn't bring it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他就是不在状态，发挥不出来。

sentences.en: And it's a reminder that, you know, we elect these people and we're electing real people who have to go into real meetings with other real people.
sentences.zh: 这提醒我们，你知道，我们选出了这些人，我们选出的是真人，他们必须与其他的真人进行真正的会面。

sentences.en: And what they say and how they behave in those actual meetings is just as important as, you know, all the policies and all the track record and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们在那些实际会面中所说的话和表现，与所有的政策、所有的政绩以及所有那些东西同样重要。

sentences.en: It comes down to the sort of behavior in that moment.
sentences.zh: 归根结底要看当时的行为表现。

sentences.en: And I mean, there are there are sort of theories about the fact that World War One may have ended very differently had Wilson been on his A-game,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一些理论认为，如果威尔逊当时处于最佳状态，第一次世界大战的结局可能会非常不同，

sentences.en: in particular with regards to what happened to Germans.
sentences.zh: 特别是关于德国人的遭遇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that Wilson really wanted was a gentle peace with Germany.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威尔逊真正想要的事情之一，就是对德国实行温和的和平。

sentences.en: He was really worried about a vindictive peace that would be about score settling because he knew that they needed to rebuild a peaceful, functioning,
sentences.zh: 他真的很担心那种旨在清算复仇的严厉和平，因为他知道他们需要重建一个和平、正常、

sentences.en: cooperative Europe after this if they were going to maintain peace beyond the end of this.
sentences.zh: 在此之后合作的欧洲，如果他们想在这场战争结束后继续维持和平的话。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was something that normally he would have pushed for.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这通常是他会极力主张的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, the flu is part of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，流感只是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: He also gets delivered a pretty devastating blow in the midterm elections of 1918 where Republicans sweep.
sentences.zh: 在1918年的中期选举中，他也遭受了相当沉重的打击，共和党取得了压倒性胜利。

sentences.en: And so there's a sense the country doesn't necessarily want everything that Wilson wants.
sentences.zh: 因此人们觉得，国家并不一定想要威尔逊想要的全部东西。

sentences.en: But, I mean, Jody, you've had the flu before.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，乔迪，你以前得过流感。

sentences.en: Can you imagine going to this table with the three other leaders of these countries and barely being able to sit up, much less, you know,
sentences.zh: 你能想象和这些国家的另外三位领导人坐在谈判桌前，却几乎连坐都坐不稳，更不用说，你知道的，

sentences.en: argue forcefully for the thing that you believe in?
sentences.zh: 有力地为你所信仰的事业辩论吗？

sentences.en: So one big question.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个重大问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this is sort of stating the obvious, but I kind of want to end on this note.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像是在陈述显而易见的事实，但我还是想以此作为结束。

sentences.en: But, like, you don't get to choose when pandemics hit.
sentences.zh: 但是，比如说，大流行什么时候爆发是选不了的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And I think it gets to this larger theme that, you know, so much of a presidency is defined by things you can't plan for.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这触及了一个更大的主题，那就是，你知道的，总统任期的很大一部分都是由那些你无法计划的事情决定的。

sentences.en: And it's really about how do you react in that moment.
sentences.zh: 关键其实在于你在那个时刻如何反应。

sentences.en: And I mean, this seems like a perfect example of that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来就是一个完美的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, the tendency at the time was the right thing to do is to downplay what's happening because people have just come through this horrifying war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时的倾向是认为正确的做法是淡化正在发生的事情，因为人们刚刚经历了这场可怕的战争。

sentences.en: The last thing that they need is to be told that there's this other invisible enemy that's going to kill millions of them.
sentences.zh: 他们最不需要的就是有人告诉他们，还有另一个会夺走他们数百万生命的看不见的敌人。

sentences.en: But, of course, what we learn from it is when you don't have a handle on it, when you don't tell people what's happening, it actually just leads to even worse outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，我们从中吸取的教训是，当你无法掌控局面，当你不如实告知人们发生了什么时，实际上只会导致更糟糕的结果。

sentences.en: And that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 事实就是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the press at the time was censoring news of this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时的媒体对这场大流行的消息进行了审查。

sentences.en: And that's not the only reason that millions and millions of people died.
sentences.zh: 这并不是千百万人死亡的唯一原因。

sentences.en: But it was a contributing factor.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个促成因素。

sentences.en: So I guess one more question on the flu itself.
sentences.zh: 所以我想再问一个关于流感本身的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, if the public had somehow known, I guess this happens relatively late that he gets it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果公众当时不知怎么知道了，我猜他感染的时候已经相对较晚了。

sentences.en: But I'm trying to imagine, you know, do these moments where like, oh, my gosh, a president got this.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在想，你知道的，这种时刻，比如说，天哪，总统感染了。

sentences.en: Do those break through?
sentences.zh: 这种消息能产生影响吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do those make a difference?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这会有所不同吗？

sentences.en: I think they do make a difference in the sense that you see that no one has the power or the money to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们确实会有所不同，因为你能看出没有人有权力或金钱来避开它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like it's one of those things that you can't negotiate your way out of.
sentences.zh: 就像这是那种你无法通过谈判来摆脱的事情。

sentences.en: Like we're all vulnerable to it.
sentences.zh: 就像我们所有人对它都是脆弱的。

sentences.en: I do think it's fair at the same time, though, that like seeing a president stricken with something like this can scare people,
sentences.zh: 不过与此同时我也觉得很公平，看到总统染上这样的疾病会让人感到恐惧，

sentences.en: particularly at a time when they're already pretty scared.
sentences.zh: 特别是当人们本来就已经很害怕的时候。

sentences.en: It can be destabilizing.
sentences.zh: 这可能会造成局势动荡。

sentences.en: There's this little meme or whatever you want to call it floating around around like people use this term of like we must protect so and so.
sentences.zh: 有个小迷因或者随便你怎么称呼的东西在流传，人们会用这种说法，比如我们必须保护某某。

sentences.en: And I think it was pre-pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我想那是在大流行之前。

sentences.en: But now people are saying, you know, we must protect, pick, you know, Beyonce or whoever.
sentences.zh: 但现在人们会说，你知道的，我们必须保护，比如，碧昂丝或者随便什么人。

sentences.en: But also, you know, politicians like we have to keep these people healthy so that they can do their jobs because their jobs have massive ramifications.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，还有政治人物，比如我们必须保持这些人健康，这样他们才能做好工作，因为他们的工作有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, let's just put it out there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们不妨直说吧。

sentences.en: Ruth Bader Ginsburg is somebody people have been trying to rap and bubble rap since three years ago.
sentences.zh: 鲁斯·巴德·金斯伯格就是那种三年前人们就想用气泡膜把它包裹起来的人。

sentences.en: And again, like it's been a powerful meme to say, like, do you want to be the person who gave this to a person who gave it to Ruth Bader Ginsburg?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是一个很有力的梗，意思是说，你想成为那个把病毒传染给传染给鲁斯·巴德·金斯伯格的人吗？

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: I hadn't really heard that framing.
sentences.zh: 我以前没听过这种说法。

sentences.en: But yeah, I guess that's something to think about.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我想这确实值得思考。

sentences.en: OK, we're going to wrap it up there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们今天就聊到这里。

sentences.en: But first, a few other things that happened on this day, April 2nd, in other years.
sentences.zh: 但首先，还有几件发生在历年4月2日的事情。

sentences.en: In 1870, the first female candidate for president, Victoria Woodhull, announced her candidacy by writing a letter to the editor of the New York Herald.
sentences.zh: 在1870年，第一位女性总统候选人维多利亚·伍德哈尔通过给《纽约先驱报》编辑写信宣布参选。

sentences.en: 1917, Janet Rankin was sworn in as the first female congressman.
sentences.zh: 1917年，珍妮特·兰金宣誓就职，成为第一位女性国会议员。

sentences.en: And in 1964, on April 2nd, Malcolm X gave his ballot or the bullet speech.
sentences.zh: 而在1964年4月2日，马尔科姆·艾克斯发表了《选票还是子弹》的演讲。

sentences.en: So every once in a while, we'll give you a taste of other things that happened on this day.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们会偶尔让你了解历史上这一天还发生过什么别的事情。

sentences.en: By the way, this is what we're doing on our social feeds as well, posting a few times a day about other things that happened.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这也是我们社交平台上在做的事情，一天发好几次关于历史上其他事情的帖子。

sentences.en: So make sure you check those out.
sentences.zh: 所以请务必去看看。

sentences.en: All right, Nicole Hemmer, thank you as always.
sentences.zh: 好了，妮可·海默，谢谢你，一如既往。

sentences.en: This was great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks, Jodi.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，乔迪。

sentences.zh: 本期《秘史政坛》是PRX电台网络Radiotopia的自豪成员。

sentences.en: Our researcher and producer is Jacob Feldman.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究员兼制作人是雅各布·费尔德曼。

sentences.zh: 如果你对即将播出的主题或日期有什么想法，请联系我们。

sentences.zh: 你可以告诉我们一个具体的日期，或者只是一个你想让我们讨论的大致主题，我们可以为它找到一个切入点。

sentences.zh: 你可以发邮件到 thisdaypod@gmail.com。

sentences.en: Next episode,
sentences.zh: 下一集，

sentences.en: we're jumping to the more recent past 2008 Barack Obama and a comment he made about rural voters that may have said a lot about where politics was going over the next decade.
sentences.zh: 我们将跳到更近的过去，即2008年巴拉克·奥巴马以及他关于农村选民的一番言论，这番言论可能在很大程度上预示了未来十年政治的发展方向。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: we've been talking about this for a couple of months and this was just going to be about the election and just use historical precedent to help describe the moment that we're in in terms of the election.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论了好几个月了，这原本只是一档关于选举的节目，仅仅利用历史先例来帮助描述我们目前所处的选举时刻。

sentences.en: And then coronavirus pandemic started and we decided to move up the launch date a week.
sentences.zh: 然后冠状病毒大流行开始了，我们决定将上线日期提前一周。

sentences.en: And so how are you thinking about the stories you will be selecting over this season while this is going on?
sentences.zh: 那么，在当前这种情况下，你是如何思考这个季节你要选择的故事的？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I do want to make space for stories, not just, oh, we're going to find stories of health crises or pandemics, but stories of just moments of national crisis.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我的确想为那些故事留出空间，不只是，哦，我们要找健康危机或大流行的故事，而是关于国家危机时刻的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we are we are in a moment, clearly, of national crisis.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我们显然正处于一个国家危机的时刻。

sentences.en: I think we are going to enter a moment of, you know, what I've been thinking of as sort of civic creativity or civic rearrangement.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将进入一个，你知道的，我一直在思考的公民创造力或公民重组的时刻。

sentences.en: We're really going to have to think through how our society is ordered and what our norms are.
sentences.zh: 我们真的必须认真思考我们的社会是如何组织以及我们的规范是什么。

sentences.en: And politics is a space in which, you know, we we do that and we've had to do that for better or worse.
sentences.zh: 政治是一个我们，你知道的，这样做并且无论好坏都必须这样做的空间。

sentences.en: And so I think making space to talk about moments where we've done that, not just necessarily linked to an election year.
sentences.zh: 所以我想留出空间来讨论我们曾经这样做过的时刻，而不仅仅是必然与选举年挂钩的时刻。

sentences.en: That said, I will I will say that my co-host, Nikki Hammer, who's a political historian, when we were talking about making this change and expanding the scope a little bit,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我还是要说，我的联合主持人妮可·海默，她是一位政治历史学家，当我们谈到做出这种改变并稍微扩大范围时，

sentences.en: she pointed out and she was like, elections have never really been normal.
sentences.zh: 她指出并表示，选举从来都不是真正的正常状态。

sentences.en: Most most elections are huge and most elections are kind of feel like they have crisis and so forth.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数选举都是规模宏大的，而且绝大多数选举都让人感觉充满危机等等。

sentences.en: And so even if we had stuck to just the election lens, we would have had plenty of big, huge moments where it felt like, oh, my gosh,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我们坚持只通过选举的镜头来看待，我们也会有很多重大时刻，让人感觉，天哪，

sentences.en: our country is tearing itself apart or being torn apart.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家正在把自己撕裂，或者正在被撕裂。

sentences.en: So, you know, I also do want to say, though, it's very important to me to also just find small moments and moments that just are interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我也想说，对我来说非常重要的一点是，也要去寻找一些微小的时刻，以及那些仅仅有趣的时刻。

sentences.en: And I think we can find lessons in those, even if we don't go out of our way to find big moments or big lessons and so forth,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以在其中找到教训，即使我们没有刻意去寻找宏大的时刻或宏大的教训等等，

sentences.en: just telling a good small story from our political past, I think will still resonate.
sentences.zh: 仅仅讲述一个来自我们政治过去的精彩小故事，我认为依然能引起共鸣。

sentences.en: And I want to make space for the esoteric.
sentences.zh: 而且我想为那些深奥冷门的内容留出空间。

sentences.en: It's not just going to be, you know, meltdowns and influenza and so forth.
sentences.zh: 不只是，你知道的，崩盘和流感之类的内容。

sentences.en: And we're going to find some some quote unquote fun and interesting stories as we go as well.
sentences.zh: 随着节目的进行，我们也会找到一些所谓有趣且引人入胜的故事。

sentences.en: And you're going to do some of that on your social media accounts and stuff like that rather than just the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且你会在你的社交媒体账号上做一些这样的事情，而不是只在播客里做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So on social media, we're going to be posting a few times a day, actually, about all the stuff that we don't get to.
sentences.zh: 所以在社交媒体上，我们实际上每天会发好几次帖子，关于所有我们来不及在节目里讲的东西。

sentences.en: We only get to do one topic per day, but we've researched a ton.
sentences.zh: 我们每天只能做一个主题，但我们做了大量的研究。

sentences.en: So just throughout the day and throughout the week on social media, on Twitter and Instagram, we're just posting about so-and-so happened this day, so-and-so happened that day.
sentences.zh: 所以在一天当中和一周当中，在社交媒体上，在Twitter和Instagram上，我们只是发帖说某某事发生在这一天，某某事发生在的那一天。

sentences.en: And I will say we've already got that going and I have found it really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我得说我们已经开始这么做了，而且我发现它真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And some of the stuff is posted.
sentences.zh: 有些东西发出去了。

sentences.en: I didn't poSt. Our producer posted.
sentences.zh: 不是我发的。是我们的制作人发的。

sentences.en: It sort of caught me off guard.
sentences.zh: 这有点让我措手不及。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: You know, on this day, we announced that we had a polio vaccine or on this day, the Navy SEALs were formed and just, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就在这一天，我们宣布我们有了脊髓灰质炎疫苗，或者就在这一天，海豹突击队成立了，然后，你知道的，

sentences.en: just little tidbits that make you stop and think and draw your own little lessons or whatever.
sentences.zh: 只是一些能让你停下来思考并得出你自己小结论之类的小花絮。

sentences.en: And so I I'm actually pretty excited about the social media stuff we've got going on as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我对我们正在进行的社交媒体内容其实也感到挺兴奋的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, you were involved.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你参与过。

sentences.en: You were in the Brian Lehrer show and you were on FiveThirtyEight.
sentences.zh: 你上过布莱恩·莱勒秀，你也上过FiveThirtyEight。

sentences.en: You often react to things in real time and are the producer and host of these discussions.
sentences.zh: 你经常对实时发生的事情作出反应，并且是这些讨论的制作人和主持人。

sentences.en: Have you missed that role during this period of time when things are happening or have you been happy to not be part of it in the direct conversation?
sentences.zh: 在这个事情频发的时期，你有没有想念过那个角色，还是说你很高兴没有直接参与到对话中？

sentences.en: I mean, I think both.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得两者都有。

sentences.en: I mean, I think anyone who is a journalist when there's a big story and someone who, you know, believes in the journalism has a role,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为任何一个在重大新闻发生时的记者，以及一个相信新闻工作有其作用的人，

sentences.en: it's been tough for me to feel a little bit like I'm sitting on the sidelines.
sentences.zh: 会觉得有点像坐在场边，对我来说这挺不容易的。

sentences.en: But I also think that stories like these looking to history, stories that kind of talk to a moment but not necessarily about a moment are really important.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，像这样回顾历史的故事，那些能够与某个时刻对话但不一定局限于某个时刻的故事，真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And so I do feel like this is my chance to engage and my chance to contribute something.
sentences.zh: 所以我的确觉得这是我参与其中并贡献力量的机会。

sentences.en: Going into this year, I sort of thought, well, do I want to cover this election again in the sort of day to day way I did for in 2016 and the three elections before that?
sentences.zh: 进入今年的时候，我曾想过，我是不是还想以2016年以及此前三次选举的那种日常方式再次报道这次选举？

sentences.en: And I basically decided, no, I mean, I like to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我基本上决定了，不，我是说，我喜欢睡觉。

sentences.en: I have a kid now.
sentences.zh: 我现在有小孩了。

sentences.en: It was like 2016, you know, took a few years off my life.
sentences.zh: 就像2016年，你知道的，让我的寿命缩短了好几年。

sentences.en: And so this feels like a good balance.
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉是一个很好的平衡。

sentences.en: This Day in Esoteric Political History is produced by Jody Avergan and Jacob Feldman.
sentences.zh: 本期《秘史政坛》由乔迪·阿维根和雅各布·费尔德曼制作。

sentences.en: It's new from Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 这是来自Radiotopia的新节目。

sentences.en: A new episode comes out every Tuesday and Thursday.
sentences.zh: 每周二和周四都会推出新的一集。

sentences.en: We'll have links to subscribe in the show notes and on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目简介和我们的网站上提供订阅链接。

sentences.en: So I have one kind of self-serving public service announcement.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个带点私心的公共服务公告。

sentences.en: Because people are not commuting as much, podcast listenership is down.
sentences.zh: 因为人们通勤减少了，播客的收听量下降了。

sentences.en: Not by much.
sentences.zh: 下降不多。

sentences.en: That's like 5% or so.
sentences.zh: 大概只有5%左右。

sentences.en: But the thing is, this is part of the economy that you can support without spending a dime.
sentences.zh: 但关键是，这是你可以不花一分钱就能支持的经济领域的一部分。

sentences.en: If you go through the 99PI catalog and download or stream just one extra episode this week, that 5% decrease will be eliminated.
sentences.zh: 如果你浏览99PI的节目目录，本周只下载或流媒体播放额外的一集，那5%的降幅就会被消除。

sentences.en: And we'll maybe even see an overall increase.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可能会看到整体的增长。

sentences.en: Or, you know, you can go download and listen to the whole omnibus and pick one episode to send to friends.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，你可以去下载并收听整个合集，然后挑选一集发给朋友。

sentences.en: People seem to really like that at-home episode I did a couple weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎真的很喜欢我几周前做的那期居家节目。

sentences.en: So maybe send that one around.
sentences.zh: 所以也许可以把那一集转发一下。

sentences.en: The point is, this is a thing where a free and joyful task could do a lot of good and keep the show healthy and strong.
sentences.zh: 重点是，这是一件免费且快乐的事情，可以做很多好事，并保持节目的健康和强大。

sentences.en: So thanks.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你们。

sentences.en: If you do heed the call and listen extra and spread the word, you know, tag me on Twitter and I'll thank you personally.
sentences.zh: 如果你听从召唤，多听一集并广为传播，你知道的，在Twitter上@我，我会亲自向你道谢。

sentences.zh: 99% Invisible 是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，在 Radio Row 制作。

sentences.en: Which is physically distributed in multiple locations, but in our heart, it's still in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 它的实体分布在多个地方，但在我们心中，它依然位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽的市中心。

sentences.en: We are a proud member of Radiotopia from PRX, a fiercely independent collective of the most innovative podcasts in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们是 PRX 旗下 Radiotopia 的自豪成员，这是一个由世界上最具创新性的播客组成的激烈独立的集体。

sentences.en: Find them all at radiotopia.fm.
sentences.zh: 请在 radiotopia.fm 上找到它们。

sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到本节目并加入关于节目的讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet me at Roman Mars and the show at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Twitter 上 @ Roman Mars，本节目的网址是 99PI.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram and Reddit too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.zh: 但你可以在 99PI.org 上浏览往期节目并与你的朋友分享。
